title: Elodie and the Cellar
premise: Theo Villalobos returns to the family farmhouse to bury her twin sister Elodie, only to discover that Elodie's body is warm and the mirrors show everything a second late — including a version of Theo who never left. The house's cellar holds an inherited song, taught mother to daughter for generations, whose final verse was deliberately lost to seal something below. As the lag between reflection and reality widens, Theo realizes Elodie crossed over first and the thing in the cellar has been wearing her sister's voice ever since. To end it, Theo must learn the song's last verse from the reflected Elodie without singing along, then bury it with her own name attached — trading her memory of Elodie entirely so the inheritance dies with her.
about_author: Jude Quintana is the pen name of a former archivist from rural New Mexico who spent a decade cataloguing estate sales and unclaimed family photographs. Their fiction explores what families preserve on purpose and what they bury by accident.

chapters.title: The Wrong Sibling
chapters.summary: Theo arrives at the farmhouse with Elodie's ashes and a notebook she fills compulsively, documenting every room as if writing could hold grief still. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: hollow ritual — she catalogs the house because feeling nothing is easier than feeling everything.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Alone in the bathroom, Theo notices her mirror reflection lags: she raises her hand, the glass follows a beat behind. She tests every mirror in the house; each one is late, and each lag grows slightly. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: creeping dread disguised as scientific curiosity.

chapters.title: What Elodie Kept
chapters.summary: Searching Elodie's locked room, Theo finds cassette tapes of their mother humming a song that stops mid-phrase, plus a ledger of names going back four generations — each entry ending with 'taught' or 'refused.' POV: Theo. Emotional beat: the discovery that grief has a paper trail.

chapters.title: The Reflected Sister
chapters.summary: The lag reaches two seconds, and in the hallway mirror Theo sees Elodie standing beside her reflection — mouthing words. When Theo turns, no one is there, but the notebook now contains handwriting that isn't hers. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: terror braided with desperate hope that her twin survived somehow.

chapters.title: Mother's Refusal
chapters.summary: A neighbor, Rosa, reveals their mother refused to teach the song's last verse and paid for it — Elodie was taken as the debt's interest. Rosa warns Theo to burn the tapes and leave. POV: Theo with Rosa's recounted memories. Emotional beat: anger at the dead for the bargains they made.

chapters.title: Singing Along
chapters.summary: Theo plays the tape and catches herself humming before she can stop; the cellar door, sealed since childhood, stands open downstairs. In the dark she hears Elodie's voice singing the missing verse — almost. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: the horror of complicity, of having already said yes.

chapters.title: The Lag Widens
chapters.summary: Now the whole house lags: sounds arrive after their causes, and Theo watches herself through windows moving a full three seconds behind. The reflected Elodie becomes clearer while the real world blurs. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: dissolution — reality and reflection trading places.

chapters.title: Down Where the Song Lives
chapters.summary: Theo descends into the cellar and finds the source: not a creature but an accumulation — every ancestor who learned the verse, folded together, wearing Elodie's face most comfortably. It offers her the last verse freely. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: seduction; the price finally named.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: In the mirror-world, Elodie — the real one, fragmenting — teaches Theo the final verse word by word, warning her to hold it silent. The thing below sings through the walls trying to make Theo harmonize. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: climax of love against appetite; holding a note you must never release.

chapters.title: Buried Under Her Own Name
chapters.summary: Theo writes the verse down, signs it, and buries the page with Elodie's ashes, surrendering every memory of her twin as payment. The mirrors sync; the house goes quiet. Epilogue: a woman lives there now who doesn't know why she cries at songs. POV: Theo, then distanced. Emotional beat: survival as amputation — the price paid in full.
